correctness.rationale: For k=floor(1/φ), n≤k+1 implies every degree ≤k and every vertex with one active neighbor adopts, so connectedness forces full propagation before and after edge insertion. For φ>1/2, only degree-one neighbors of the single seed activate in the first step and cannot trigger further activation, so at most two active leaves are lost under one added edge; a star plus added edge between leaves attains loss 2. For φ≤1/2 and n≥k+2, the explicit gate tree starts full cascade through a degree-k vertex and degree≤2 path, while adding a single incident edge raises the gate to degree k+1, preventing any first adoption; loss n−1 is globally maximal. Checks address reciprocal thresholds and integer boundary cases; 25 independently simulated rational witnesses matched exact formulas. Proof is universal, not inferred from simulations.
residual_risks: Only one permanently active seed, connected simple undirected graphs and synchronous deterministic irreversible common fractional thresholds are covered.
